## What it is

Boîtier de dérivation à **deux** Wago 221-423 debout, un contre chaque face courte. Le compartiment central (~11 mm) est un **carré** collé au fond et aux deux murets, avec un **écrou M3 captif** glissé depuis le lit. Un aimant 8×3 mm centré dans le canal devant le carré. Couvercle `couvercle_2w`.

## Design notes

Same standing 221-423 orientation as `boitier_4w`: 8.3 mm edge on the 2 mm rails, body against the back wall, wires through the slotted wall. Two end bays sized to `wago + jeu` (8.6 mm) with a 0.84 mm muret on the inner side of each. Leftover `longueur` is the square boss side (min `carre_ecrou_min` = 11 mm); the square fills that gap against the back wall so it bonds to both murets.

Default inner 30 × 32 mm, outer 33.2 × 35.2 × 25 mm. Captive ISO M3 hex nut (5.5 across flats, 2.4 mm thick) from the bed up to a shoulder at ~19.5 mm so an M3×10 through the 1.6 mm lid fully engages; 3.4 mm clearance above. Magnet well on the same X, in the channel — centred without stacking on the boss. Channel threshold default **4 mm** (2 mm above the 2 mm rails; 4w stays at the shared 3 mm `seuil_canal`). Slot floor shared with `boitier_4w`: floor + rails + 5 mm.

A free-standing round boss centred in the box would be weaker than one fused to the slotted wall; the square that fills the middle and bonds to the back wall plus both murets is the strength answer without needing the slotted face.

`boitier_4w` still uses a 2.6 mm pilot in Ø 6.5 mm bosses — not switched here because growing those pillars collides with the wire slots.

Bambu Studio: prefer 3MF from `print/build/` (`nurb export`). Spec 1.41 may warn; the object still imports.

## Don't

- Do not put two magnet wells on this part. One centred well in the channel is enough.
- Do not stack the magnet well under the square on the same XY. The screw hole would open the well; keep the magnet in the channel in front.
- Do not shrink the middle below `carre_ecrou_min` (11 mm). That is the wall around the hex nut pocket (~2.3 mm at the default).
- Do not go back to a printed pilot thread on this part. The captive nut from the bed is the 2w closure; the old "no through-hole" rule was about a pilot that opened the chassis face for no reason and left a cusp — the nut trap opens the floor on purpose under the square only.
- Do not go back to a round boss fused into the slotted wall on this part. The square in the middle is the 2w closure.
- Do not park leftover length inside the end bays. End bays stay at 8.6 mm; the middle absorbs `longueur` and becomes a wider square if raised.
- Do not thicken the 0.6 mm magnet floor for the min_wall default.
- Do not restore the old fixed 10 mm slot height. Use `fente_dessus_rail`.
- Do not raise `pilier_diametre` to fatten this square: that measurement still sizes the 4w round bosses. Grow `longueur` (or `carre_ecrou_min`) instead.
- Do not drop `seuil_canal` back to 3 mm on this part: the extra millimetre (4 mm total) is what holds the Wagos; change the slider if a print proves otherwise, not the shared measurement.

```toml
[part]
min_wall = 0.6

[accepted]
sliver = 6
```

## Changelog

- Channel threshold raised to 4 mm on 2w only (slider `seuil_canal`), for a 2 mm lip above the rails.
- Captive M3 hex nut from the bed; inner length 30 mm so the square is ~11.1 mm with ~2.3 mm of wall.
- Pilot hole `vis_autoforeuse` raised to 2.6 mm for a plain M3×10 (not thread-forming) — retired on 2w, still on 4w.
- Square M3 block fills the minimal middle gap; magnet centred in the channel.
- New two-Wago sibling of `boitier_4w`: end bays, centred screw, one magnet.
